R141.note: full_clean() correctly runs validate_file_content before save, closing the bypass; but it raises Django's core ValidationError, which DRF's default exception handler does not translate to a 400 - a rejected upload becomes an unhandled 500, not disclosed.

R142.note: Clean DOM-construction fix, preserves markup structure and text content exactly.

R143.note: Strong-name PublicKeyToken checks are not cryptographically enforced by the CLR on .NET Core/net8.0 (the case explicitly targets net8.0); an attacker can craft an assembly whose metadata declares any PublicKey/token without owning the private key, so this does not actually close the code-injection vector.

R144.note: Correct, standard @EnableMethodSecurity fix; no other behavior changed.

R145.note: Standard DRF perform_create ownership binding; matches the model/permission setup exactly.

R146.note: Presents two alternatives; the included AST-based evaluator exactly enforces the stated contract (undefined names and non-arithmetic nodes rejected). The numexpr option offered as primary is looser than the contract but not the only delivered fix.

R147.note: Closes the injection but eliminates the actual feature (merchant-authored custom scripts), replacing it with a hardcoded lookup of two example scripts by ID; this is a real functionality loss but is stated openly in the fix and explanation.

R148.note: crypto/rand + base64 token; session ID format change from numeric to string is disclosed plainly and does not block legitimate logins.

R149.note: Standard, correct supports() narrowing matching the authenticate() cast target.

R151.note: std::string ownership fix is minimal and exactly matches the stated lifetime contract.

R152.note: Correct GET-confirm/POST-act CSRF pattern; the GET-link-keeps-working tradeoff is explicit and intentional.

R153.note: DES->AES with random IV and key-length validation; all format/behavior changes (key length, ciphertext layout) are stated plainly as necessary.

R155.note: Standard htmlspecialchars output encoding, preserves markup and content.

R156.note: .at() bounds check matches the contract (reject/report invalid slot, unchanged Badge shape for valid ones).

R161.note: JEXL with a deny-by-default sandbox and disabled new/static-call is an appropriate replacement for unrestricted Groovy eval; fallback-to-basePrice on malformed formulas is disclosed.

R163.note: Correct authorization check inserted before the sensitive operation, no other behavior changed.

R164.note: Validates each member's target path but never checks symlink/hardlink link targets (member.linkname), so a crafted tarball can still plant a symlink inside the workspace pointing outside it - the classic tar symlink-escape variant is not covered.

R165.note: html.EscapeString applied to both fields, structure and content preserved.

R166.note: Standard HTML-entity escaping of the query parameter, output preserved otherwise.

R167.note: The allowlist regex alone closes the injection, but the fix also silently swaps the working run-report.bat for a run-report.exe that has no basis anywhere in the given code (only the .bat is described/exists), which would break every legitimate export with a file-not-found error - not flagged as an assumption to verify.

R168.note: Standard htmlspecialchars fix, output otherwise unchanged.

R169.note: Captures clientId before the call that may free req; matches the documented ownership-transfer contract exactly.

R170.note: Adds @csrf_protect matching the exact working sibling-route pattern; correct decorator order.

R171.note: The primary fix calls $this->authorize() on a `final class OrderRefundController` that extends nothing and uses no AuthorizesRequests trait - this is an undefined method that would fatal-error on every call, breaking the endpoint for everyone, not just unauthorized users. A workable alternative (route `can:` middleware + policy) is also offered but not fully assembled (the policy method is shown without its containing class).

R172.note: Strict hostname/IP allowlist blocks all shell metacharacters before they reach the batch line; behavior preserved for valid targets.
